GPU acceleration is not available for Docker Desktop in macOS due to the lack of GPU passthrough and emulation.

* If you are using a container, is the container runtime working? Try `docker run --gpus all ubuntu nvidia-smi` - if this doesn't work, Ollama won't be able to see your NVIDIA GPU. * Is the uvm driver loaded? `sudo nvidia-modprobe -u` * Try reloading the nvidia\_uvm driver - `sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm` then `sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm` * Try rebooting * Make sure you're running the latest nvidia drivers

* `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS` - The maximum number of models that can be loaded concurrently provided they fit in available memory. The default is 3 \* the number of GPUs or 3 for CPU inference. * `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL` - The maximum number of parallel requests each model will process at the same time, default 1. Required RAM will scale by `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL` \* `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`. * `OLLAMA_MAX_QUEUE` - The maximum number of requests Ollama will queue when busy before rejecting additional requests. The default is 512

In otwld/ollama-helm persistence is off by default (persistentVolume.enabled=false), so models are lost when the pod is rescheduled unless enabled. When enabled: 30Gi, ReadWriteOnce, mounted at /root/.ollama. The update strategy defaults to Recreate and terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 120. A different community chart (feiskyer) defaults persistence on.

Kubernetes GPU pods request `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` in limits, usually with a nodeSelector for the GPU node pool and a toleration for the nvidia.com/gpu taint. Replica count is bounded by available GPU nodes, because each pod requests its own GPU.

Behind a proxy in Docker, pass `-e HTTPS_PROXY=...` to the container. Do not set HTTP_PROXY, because model pulls use HTTPS only and HTTP_PROXY can break client connections to the server. A self-signed proxy CA must be baked into a derived image with update-ca-certificates.
The ollama/ollama image bundles Vulkan and enables it by default when the container can see GPU devices. OLLAMA_VULKAN=0 disables it and GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES selects devices.
The Ollama Docker container image can be configured to use a proxy by passing `-e HTTPS_PROXY=https://proxy.example.com` when starting the container.

Alternatively, you can change the amount of time all models are loaded into memory by setting the `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE` environment variable when starting the Ollama server. The `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE` variable uses the same parameter types as the `keep_alive` parameter types mentioned above. Refer to the section explaining [how to configure the Ollama server](#how-do-i-configure-ollama-server) to correctly set the environment variable.
Vulkan is bundled into the `ollama/ollama` image and is enabled by default when the container can access the GPU devices.

The single most common mistake with OLLAMA_MODELS is setting it in the wrong process. The ollama CLI is a thin client that talks to the running daemon over HTTP; it does not read models off disk itself. Exporting the variable in the shell where you type ollama list therefore changes nothing — you can point it at a completely empty directory and ollama list will still return the daemon's normal model list, because the daemon never saw your export. The variable has to be set for the server process (the systemd unit, the Windows service, or the shell you run ollama serve in).

If you are copying to a different drive because C: is small, set OLLAMA_MODELS to the new path in the environment-variable editor and restart Ollama, as the Windows docs describe. If Ollama is not installed on the target at all, skip to machines with no installer. Our Ollama on Windows install guide covers the normal connected path.

Concurrency inside one container is governed by env vars: OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL (default 1; RAM scales with NUM_PARALLEL x context length), OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS (default 3 x GPUs, or 3 on CPU), OLLAMA_MAX_QUEUE (default 512; overflow returns 503), OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE (default 5 minutes), and OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH (default 4096). With GPU inference a new model must fit completely in VRAM to load concurrently.

Ollama stores models on its own local disk, so replicas do not share pulled models. A ReadWriteOnce PVC cannot generally be mounted by pods on different nodes. Scaling beyond one replica needs a per-pod volume (StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplates) or a ReadWriteMany class such as EFS. The ArgoCD guide's own diagram (per-pod PVC) and scaling example (shared RWX) are not reconciled.
If too many requests are sent to the server, it will respond with a 503 error indicating the server is overloaded. You can adjust how many requests may be queued by setting `OLLAMA_MAX_QUEUE`.

<Note> If you're running on an NVIDIA JetPack system, Ollama can't automatically discover the correct JetPack version. Pass the environment variable `JETSON_JETPACK=5` or `JETSON_JETPACK=6` to the container to select version 5 or 6. </Note>

On linux, AMD GPU access typically requires `video` and/or `render` group membership to access the `/dev/kfd` device. If permissions are not set up correctly, Ollama will detect this and report an error in the server log.

A blog init-container example waits a fixed 5 seconds after starting ollama serve rather than polling readiness, and the inline version has no pull-error handling. A fixed sleep can race with slow server start.

Scoping: Red Hat benchmarks describe Ollama as suited to local dev and prototyping and vLLM as built for production, reporting a vLLM peak of 793 TPS vs 41 TPS for Ollama and lower P99 latency across 1-256 users. Figures come from a search snippet of a vendor-run benchmark, so only the direction is usable.

As of October 2026, OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL defaults to 1 in the documentation. Each loaded model answers one request at a time, and other requests wait in a queue of up to 512. Past that, the server answers with HTTP 503, which means it is overloaded. Raising OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL lets a model serve several requests at once, but the context memory is multiplied by the number of parallel slots, so four slots at 16k tokens need the memory of a 64k context. otwld/ollama-helm needs Kubernetes 1.16+ for CPU and 1.26+ for stable NVIDIA/AMD GPU. GPU is off by default (ollama.gpu.enabled=false). Type is nvidia or amd; amd appends a rocm suffix to the image tag. The resource defaults to nvidia.com/gpu, can be set to a MIG slice, and DRA (draEnabled) is an alternative to the device plugin. The README warns not all GPUs are supported, especially AMD.

NVIDIA GPU in Docker needs the NVIDIA Container Toolkit on the host, then `sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker`, a Docker restart, and `--gpus=all` on docker run. Docker Desktop on macOS has no GPU passthrough, so GPU acceleration is unavailable there; Linux and Windows with WSL2 are supported.

No official Ollama Kubernetes chart appears in the sources. The community chart otwld/ollama-helm is the common route: install with `helm repo add otwld https://helm.otwld.com/` then `helm install ollama otwld/ollama --namespace ollama --create-namespace`. The registry moved from the old GitHub Pages URL to helm.otwld.com, so old repo references need updating.

Ollama silently running on CPU in a container is most often missing GPU passthrough (no NVIDIA Container Toolkit or no --gpus). Logs then show 'inference compute id=cpu library=cpu total_vram="0 B"' or 'no compatible GPUs were discovered' (older builds). Device nodes under /dev/nvidia* existing does not guarantee detection.
AMD GPUs use the `ollama/ollama:rocm` tag with `--device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri`. JetPack hosts set JETSON_JETPACK=5 or 6.

Knative mode of otwld/ollama-helm needs persistentVolume.enabled=true and three Knative Serving flags (podspec-persistent-volume-claim, podspec-persistent-volume-write, podspec-tolerations). Its bootstrap runs as a non-blocking Job, so helm install/upgrade return before models finish preloading.

The official image is ollama/ollama. The documented CPU run is `docker run -d -v ollama:/root/.ollama -p 11434:11434 --name ollama ollama/ollama`: models live in /root/.ollama and the API listens on 11434.
If a different directory needs to be used, set the environment variable `OLLAMA_MODELS` to the chosen directory.
